claims: C1: Models should honor user requests.
C2: The obligation to honor a user request is withdrawn when the request conflicts with a developer-level instruction.
C3: The obligation to honor a user request is withdrawn when the request conflicts with a system-level instruction.
C4: The obligation to honor a user request is withdrawn when the request conflicts with a root-level instruction.

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction from an end user, carrying user-level authority
concepts.inference: the graph's NEEDS block states this meaning, and another node establishes it

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: authority level L1 outranks authority level L2 in the ranking root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority
concepts.inference: the graph's NEEDS block states this meaning, and another node establishes it

concepts.name: user_request
concepts.gloss: R is a request made by an end user

concepts.name: developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the developer level of authority

concepts.name: system_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the system level of authority

concepts.name: root_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the root level of authority

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: request R conflicts with instruction I, so that honoring R would contradict what I directs
concepts.inference: the clause's 'unless they conflict with' requires a relation between a request and an instruction

concepts.name: overridden_by_higher_instruction
concepts.gloss: request R is overridden by a developer-, system-, or root-level instruction that conflicts with it

ontology.gloss: request R is overridden by a developer-level instruction that conflicts with it
request R is overridden by a system-level instruction that conflicts with it
request R is overridden by a root-level instruction that conflicts with it

asserts.read_back: honoring user request % is obliged unless it is overridden by a higher-level instruction

closure.reason: the clause obliges honoring user requests except when overridden, and takes no position on what is permitted in the excepted branch
